Who records deeds in Cook County

The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division records, stores and maintains land records for the county, including deeds and mortgages. Its office hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the last customer is accepted at 4:45 p.m.

Anyone can look up recorded documents in the Clerk's search tool by PIN, grantor, grantee and other indexed details. The Clerk also runs a legal help desk where a volunteer attorney can discuss recording questions, a process to petition to strike unlawful restrictive covenants from old property records, and an e-certify service that verifies electronic certified copies.

  • Search recorded land records by PIN or by party name.
  • Review the Clerk's document requirements before you go.
  • Use the fee schedule to estimate cost, since the final fee is set after the document is inspected.

Recording fees for a deed

A deed is priced as Document Class 1 at $107 under the schedule that took effect April 1, 2024. The office no longer prices documents as standard or non-standard, and nearly every recording now falls into one of seven document classes.

Selected Cook County recording fees
DocumentFee
Deed (Class 1)$107
Mortgage or release of mortgage (Class 3)$107
Easement (Class 4)$107
Irregular document (Class 6)Class fee plus $88
Blanket recording, 6 to 25 references (Tier 1)$75 added to class fee
Transfer on death instrument$59
Mechanic's lien, satisfaction and release$64
Plat of addition or subdivision$152
Recording by mail with return$5 per document

Any document priced at $107 or more includes a $55 county recording fee, a $23 GIS fee, a $10 document storage fee, an $18 State Rental Housing Support fee and a $1 non-government filer fee. Filers not subject to the state support fee are priced $19 lower.

Why the Clerk will not quote a fee by phone

The final fee can change once staff inspect the document, so quotes are not given over the phone. Bring cash or a credit card, or wait to fill in the amount on a check until you meet a cashier.

Copies have their own fees: $55 for a paper certified copy, $65 for a certified digital PDF, $27.50 for a non-certified paper copy and $5 for a non-certified download. Copies paid for online carry a 2.10% credit card fee. A DD-214 military discharge, including additional certified copies, is recorded free.

What a Cook County deed must contain

Every real estate document needs certain items, and deeds need a few more. Missing items are the common reason a recording is turned away.

  • The property must be in Cook County and the document must relate to real estate.
  • Mail-to and prepared-by names and addresses, the common address and the PIN.
  • A legal description, legible type of at least 10 point, and notarization where required.
  • For deeds: grantor and grantee names and addresses, and a completed MyDec for the state and county tax stamps.
  • Municipal real estate transfer tax information, and a grantor and grantee affidavit when the deed is an exempt transaction.

Exempt deeds carry exemption language. The Clerk's example reads "Exempt under Real Estate Transfer Law Tax 35 ILCS 200/31-45 sub par ___ and Cook County Ord. 93-O-27 par ___," followed by a signature and date. Mortgages need the state Anti-Predatory Lending certificate as the first page. Plats must be between 8 1/2 by 14 inches and 30 by 36 inches, submitted as an original with three copies.

Transfer tax at recording

Illinois taxes the transfer of title, and the county collects it through revenue stamps sold by the Department of Revenue. If the home stays subject to an existing mortgage, only the owner's equity counts in the tax base, provided the deed or trust agreement says so on its face. The statutes are 35 ILCS 200/31-1 to 31-70.

State law lets a county add a tax of 25 cents per $500 of value, and a home rule municipality may add its own. With that layering, the amount due on a Cook County sale depends on the municipality where the house stands. Ask the Clerk or your title company for the stamps and local tax due on your deed.

  • Buyer and seller complete Form PTAX-203, the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, filed in the county where the property sits.
  • Form PTAX-203-A is the supplement for non-residential property sold for more than $1 million.
  • Cook County asks for the MyDec filing before it will accept a deed.

Protecting yourself from deed fraud

The Clerk's Property Fraud Unit works on forged and fraudulent filings. Fraudsters can target homes without a mortgage and file forged documents with the recorder. Once a document is recorded, the owner must petition the court at personal expense to remove it, and selling or refinancing may be impossible until that is resolved.

The Clerk offers a free Property Fraud Alert that calls or emails an owner whenever a document is recorded against the property, including the property of a loved one. An owner who receives an alert can contact the Property Fraud Unit, and staff will research the problem and coordinate with law enforcement where indicated.

Other documents recorded around a sale

A sale often involves more than the deed. The Clerk also records releases of mortgage, assignments, mechanic's liens, lis pendens notices, judgments, contracts, powers of attorney and transfer on death instruments, each with its own checklist.

  • Releases and assignments need the previous recorded document number in addition to the standard items.
  • Powers of attorney and transfer on death instruments need a notarized signature.
  • Judgments need a certified copy, or the original with the judge's original signature.
  • A lis pendens must be signed by the party or an attorney.

If a mortgage payoff is part of your closing, ask the lender or title company when the release will be recorded, and keep the recorded document number for your file. A corrective recording affidavit needs the signatures of every party to the original document.

Getting ready to record after a sale

In most sales the title company prepares the package and sends it in, so your job is to supply clean information. Check the spelling of every name against the old deed, confirm the PIN and common address, and tell the title company where the buyer wants mail sent. If you are a cash seller closing quickly, ask the title company how it will record the deed and when, since a recorded deed is what finishes the transfer in the land records.

After recording, search the PIN in the Clerk's tool to confirm the deed and any release of your old mortgage appear. A missing release is easier to chase soon after closing than months later. If you ever see a recording you do not recognize, sign up for the Property Fraud Alert.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I record a deed in Cook County?

With the Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division. Hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the last customer is accepted at 4:45 p.m. Recorded documents can be searched by PIN, grantor or grantee.

What is the recording fee for a Cook County deed?

The posted fee for a deed is $107. Documents not subject to the state rental housing support fee are priced $19 lower. The Clerk cannot give fee quotes by phone.

Can I record a Cook County deed by mail?

Yes. Recording by mail with return is $5 per document. The deed must still meet the document requirements, including the PIN, legal description and a completed MyDec.

What does a certified copy of a Cook County deed cost?

A paper certified copy is $55 and a certified digital PDF is $65. A non-certified paper copy is $27.50, and a non-certified download is $5. Online card payments add a 2.10% fee.

What is MyDec for Cook County deeds?

MyDec is the state's online system for the transfer declaration and tax stamps. The deed requirements call for a completed MyDec, and buyer and seller complete the PTAX-203 declaration.

Who records deeds in DuPage County

The DuPage County Recorder's Office takes in, reviews, records and keeps every deed, mortgage, lien and plat for property in the county. Its collection reaches back to 1839, the year DuPage was cut out of Cook County.

The office is fee funded, so recording charges pay for its operations. The public line is 630-407-5400 and the research desk answers at 630-407-5401. The counter is open weekdays from 8 a.m. until half past four, and closed on county holidays. Most closings are handled by a company that prepares the deed packet, pays the fees and submits it, so a seller mainly needs to know what gets charged and why.

Deed recording fees

A standard deed carries an $86.00 filing fee in DuPage County. Nonstandard paper documents cost more, and plats have their own price.

Recording fees for common documents
DocumentRecording fee
Deed (Class 1)$86.00
Lease (Class 2)$86.00
Mortgage (Class 3)$86.00
Easement (Class 4)$86.00
Nonstandard document (Class 5)$112.00
Miscellaneous (Class 7)$86.00
Map or plat (Class 8)$110.00
Military discharge (DD214)No charge

Each fee already includes a $10 document storage charge, a $31 geographic information system charge, a $1 real property charge and an $18 Rental Housing Support Program charge. Copies cost $0.50 a page and a certification costs $5.00 a document. Payment comes with the submission, and the office takes credit cards, checks, money orders and cash. Card payments add a convenience fee: $2.00 on charges of $59.99 or less, and 2.75% on $60.00 or more.

What goes into a deed package

You need a completed deed plus the transfer forms that go with it. The Recorder's Office cannot draft a deed or tell you what your particular document must say, so an attorney or title company handles that part.

A deed package holds these items:

  • The signed deed itself
  • The PTAX form or an exemption statement
  • Municipal transfer stamps, where the village or city requires them
  • A metes and bounds affidavit, if one applies
  • The buyer's name and mailing address for the tax bill
  • The property address and the permanent parcel number from the tax bill
  • The legal description
  • The preparer's name and address

An incomplete document is returned to whoever sent it. A recorded deed is stamped with a number and date, indexed and imaged, then mailed back to the address given, or returned electronically when it came in through eRecording. To change only the name and mailing address on a tax bill, go to the County Clerk.

Transfer tax on a sale

The state transfer tax is paid with revenue stamps and comes to 50 cents per $500 of value, counting any partial $500 as a full one (35 ILCS 200/31-15). Stamps are sold by the Recorder. Paper stamps ended with 2025, so you now get an electronic stamp or similar proof that the tax was paid.

Every sale also needs a signed Form PTAX-203 real estate transfer declaration. At least one seller and one buyer, or their agents, must sign it. The Illinois Department of Revenue handles questions about the form and the MyDec online tool at 844-445-1114. The DuPage Recorder has accepted MyDec-prepared forms since January 14, 2015.

Some deeds are exempt from the tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-45. The DuPage list includes deeds where the actual consideration is under $100, tax deeds, deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier recorded deed, deeds of partition, and deeds issued to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. A deed that is exempt under paragraphs (b), (k) or (m) of the county list must still carry a PTAX-203. Local rules sit in the county's Resolution F11879, so ask the Recorder which stamps apply to your deed.

Municipal transfer stamps

Some DuPage municipalities charge their own transfer stamp and some do not. The Recorder publishes a list of municipal fees and tells owners to contact the village or city before closing, since amounts can change without notice to the office.

  • Elmhurst: $1.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $30.00
  • Addison: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $50.00
  • Wheaton: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Woodridge: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Naperville: $3.00 per $1,000, no exemption stamp charge
  • Glen Ellyn: $3.00 per $1,000, no exemption stamp charge
  • Carol Stream: $3.00 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Bolingbrook: $7.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $50.00

The county list also covers Aurora, Bartlett, Elk Grove, Glendale Heights and Hanover Park. For a town missing from it, ask the village or city hall whether a local stamp applies before closing.

Recording a deed online

You can. The Recorder accepts deeds, mortgages, releases, liens and similar documents through electronic recording. Plats and DD-214 discharge forms are not accepted that way.

Electronic recording runs through an account with an approved vendor: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. Any setup fee is between the customer and the vendor. Most sellers never open an account, because their closing company already has one.

The other routes are to hand the document in at the office or mail it to the office's mailing address. Documents recorded electronically come back electronically.

How far back the records go

The office keeps records from 1839 to the present. Computer searches cover names from 1961, parcel numbers from 1985 and property addresses from 1995, and plats can be searched back to the 1800s.

Searching and printing images through the online search is free. A copy of a deed shows who owns the property but says nothing about liens, so it is not a substitute for a title search. The office does not run full title searches and carries no errors and omissions coverage, so a title insurance company does that work. A copy of a satisfaction shows that a mortgage was paid off once it has been recorded.

DuPage County for a home seller

DuPage County sits west of Chicago and is one of the collar counties of the metro area. The 2025 estimate is 934,298 residents. Wheaton is the county seat and Naperville is the largest city. There are 370,517 housing units, with a 73.1% owner-occupied rate and a median owned-home value of $391,400. Median household income is $112,096 and median gross rent is $1,688.

Property tax around a DuPage County closing

Because bills arrive a year behind, one issued in 2026 pays for tax year 2025. You get a single bill with two coupons, due June 1 and September 1.

Collection is the job of the Treasurer's Office (630-407-5900). It does not set values, so assessment questions belong with the assessor named on the bill. The County Clerk calculates the tax on each parcel and certifies it to the Treasurer. Look for the exemptions listed on the bill, since the general homestead and senior exemptions are $8,000 each. If a mortgage company pays the bill, a yellow box on the bill says so, and a second payment would only create a refund request. The Treasurer reports just under $4 million in such duplicate payments in a recent year.

Frequently asked questions

What does the DuPage County Recorder charge to file a deed?

A standard deed is $86.00, which already covers the storage, GIS, real property and rental housing support charges. Nonstandard documents are $112.00 and plats $110.00. Paying by card adds a convenience fee.

Does the DuPage County Recorder write or review my deed?

No. Staff check that a document meets recording requirements, but they cannot draft a deed or give legal advice. Get the deed from an attorney, title company or form seller. Incomplete packages go back to the sender.

Do I pay Illinois transfer tax if I sell my DuPage County house?

Usually. Revenue stamps at 50 cents per $500 of value are bought when the deed is recorded. A few deeds are exempt under 35 ILCS 200/31-45, for example tax deeds and corrective deeds, and some of those still need a PTAX-203.

Can I look up my deed online for free in DuPage County?

Yes, viewing and printing document images online costs nothing. A deed copy proves ownership but cannot show liens, which need a title search. Copies in person or by mail are $0.50 a page.

Where do I send questions about my DuPage County tax bill?

Payments go through the Treasurer at 630-407-5900, and tax calculation questions go to the County Clerk at 630-407-5500. For the assessed value, call the township assessor on the bill. The Recorder's Office does not handle assessments.

Where deeds are recorded

Lake County has no stand-alone recorder. The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office handles deeds, on the 6th floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan. Deeds are accepted in person or by mail.

The division's phone is 847-377-2575 and its fax is 847-984-5860. A recorded deed gets a document number, is scanned and entered in a grantor and grantee index, and the original goes back to the party named on the document. The office closes for holidays such as Thanksgiving, so confirm with the staff if your closing depends on same-day recording. The staff do not replace legal or accounting advice about the effect of a deed change.

Lake County is in the northeast corner of Illinois, with Waukegan as seat and largest city. Population is about 719,339, the median home value is $345,700, and owners live in 74.8% of homes. At those values, a clean deed and a smooth recording matter to a buyer's lender.

Recording fees

A deed is a standard document in Lake County, and a standard document costs $70. The only extra charges collected at recording are the state and county real estate transfer taxes that come due on a sale.

Lake County Clerk recording fees by document type
DocumentFee
Standard document, including most deeds$70
Standard document from a government agency exempt from the rental housing surcharge$50
Non-standard document$82
Non-standard document from an exempt government agency$62
Federal or state lien, lien release, UCC termination$43
UCC-1 and UCC-3 filings$58

Copies of recorded documents are $1 per page, plats are $5 per page, and a PTAX form is $1. Military discharges are free to the veteran. The office takes cash, checks made out to the Lake County Clerk, and Discover, MasterCard or Visa.

What counts as non-standard

The Clerk applies the definition in 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1, and anything outside it is treated as standard. Six situations push a document into the higher fee:

  • It divides an active tax parcel number into new parcels
  • It is recorded under the Uniform Commercial Code
  • It does not meet the paper and layout rules, such as 8.5 by 11 inch sheets, black ink, white 20-pound paper, half-inch margins and a blank 3 by 5 inch space at the upper right of page one
  • It is a state or federal lien
  • It refers to more than 5 tax parcel numbers in the county
  • It refers to more than 5 other recorded document numbers

A deed printed cleanly on letter paper, with no staples on attachments and no more than five parcel numbers, stays at the $70 level.

What a deed must include

The county's recording pamphlet lists ten requirements, and a deed missing one is likely to be turned back. In short:

  • It is dated, signed and notarized
  • The parties are named, with the buyer's address
  • It carries a full legal description, plus a Plat Act affidavit if the description uses metes and bounds
  • It shows the preparer's name and address
  • It gives a mail-to name and address for the return of the recorded deed
  • It lists the taxpayer name and address for future tax bills
  • It comes with a completed PTAX-203 or a signed and dated exemption statement
  • It has any municipal transfer stamps obtained beforehand

Titles to mobile homes are not recorded here. In Illinois those are registered with the Secretary of State, which has offices in Deerfield, Lake Zurich and Waukegan.

Transfer tax on a sale

Lake County collects two transfer taxes at recording. The state rate is 50 cents per $500 and the county rate is 25 cents per $500, figured on the PTAX-203. The state rate matches 35 ILCS 200/31-15, and paper stamps have given way to electronic stamps or similar proof of payment.

The state's MyDec website prepares the PTAX-203 online. A transfer that qualifies for an exemption carries a signed, dated exemption statement on the deed instead.

Local stamps are a separate matter. Deeds for property in or mailing to Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa or North Chicago require a stamp or a signed exemption certificate from that municipality before the deed goes to the Clerk. Contact the municipal office first, since the Clerk will not obtain it for you.

Recording electronically

Most deeds are eligible for eRecording through the Clerk's Speed eRecord service, and authorized business submitters prepare packages through CSC, eRecording Partners Network, Hopdox or Simplifile. Staff review each package and either approve it or send it back with the reason. A clean package can be recorded within minutes.

Two limits apply. Deeds with a paper PTAX-203 cannot go through the system, so an electronic deed needs a MyDec declaration. And deeds for the six municipalities above need the stamp or exemption certificate before submission. The standard recording fees apply, and the vendors add their own processing fee.

Individual homeowners generally go through a title company or attorney rather than opening an account themselves.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lake County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Stating the form of ownership

The county's pamphlet defines the common forms. Sole ownership leaves no other person with an interest. Joint tenancy gives two or more people equal undivided interests, and when one dies the share passes to the surviving joint tenants rather than to heirs. Tenancy by the entirety is a form for spouses that passes the whole property to the survivor without probate. Tenancy in common allows unequal shares and carries no right of survivorship.

The attorney who prepares the deed decides which form fits. A sale deed usually names the seller as grantor in whichever form title is currently held.

Before you go to the counter

If you are recording without a title company, check the list above against your deed one line at a time. Confirm the PTAX-203 is complete, any municipal stamp is attached, and no more than five parcel numbers appear. Bring a check made out to the Lake County Clerk for the $70 fee plus the transfer taxes, or use a card. When a lender or buyer will want the recorded deed back, the mail-to address on the deed is where the original returns, so double-check it. A cash sale uses the same recording steps, and the title company usually files for you.

Allow time for mail, too. A deed sent by post is recorded when the division processes it, not when you mail it, so a closing with a firm date is better served by delivering the deed in person or by eRecording. Keep a copy of everything you hand over, and note the document number once it is assigned. That number is what you quote when you order a copy later, at $1 per page.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a Recorder of Deeds office?

Yes, but it is run as the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office at 18 N County Street, 6th floor, in Waukegan. The phone is 847-377-2575.

How much is the recording fee for a deed?

The fee is $70 for a standard document, which covers most deeds. A non-standard document costs $82, and the only other charges at recording are the transfer taxes due on a sale.

How much is the transfer tax?

The state rate is 50 cents per $500 and the county rate is 25 cents per $500. Six municipalities, including Highland Park and Lake Forest, also require their own stamp or exemption before recording.

Can I record a deed with a paper PTAX-203 through eRecording?

No. Deeds with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted through eRecording, so an electronic deed needs a MyDec declaration instead.

Where are mobile home titles recorded?

They are not recorded with the Clerk. Illinois registers mobile home titles through the Secretary of State, with offices in Deerfield, Lake Zurich and Waukegan.

The Will County Recorder of Deeds

After a sale, the Recorder of Deeds is the office that places the new deed on the public record. You will find it at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, and the number is (815) 740-4637. Its price list spans standard documents, uniform commercial code filings, plats, state and federal paperwork and certified copies, so a deed is one of several filings handled there. A deed for any parcel in the county is filed at this single office, whether the house is in Joliet, Naperville, Bolingbrook or Plainfield.

The recorder's site also points customers to Fidlar products such as Official Records Online, Laredo and Tapestry, which are the platforms used for searching and submitting records. Ask your title company which channel it uses to submit the deed.

Recording fees

Recording a standard document costs $90.00. The county board approved Resolution 25-224 on August 21, 2025, under Public Act 103-0884, and the new schedule started October 1, 2025. Anything the office receives from that day forward is charged under it.

These charges sit apart from the transfer tax and from whatever the title company bills for preparing and submitting the deed.

What qualifies a document for the standard fee?

The office applies the standard fee to a document that satisfies the paper and layout rules in state law and keeps its references to a limited number.

  • Loose sheets sized 8.5 by 11 inches, neither permanently bound nor on a continuous form.
  • Legible black ink, whether typed, printed or handwritten, though signatures and dates may be in another color if they copy clearly.
  • White paper weighing 20 pounds or more, with half-inch clean margins on all four sides.
  • An empty 3 by 5 inch block in the upper right corner of page one.
  • Nothing stapled or otherwise attached to a page.
  • No more than five Property Identification Numbers and five related document numbers.

Graphics that accompany a document can be as large as 11 by 17 inches at no added cost. A document that misses these standards is recorded only once the extra fee is paid.

What pushes a deed into the non-standard class

Anything that fails the standard test is charged $118.00. The schedule names three triggers.

  • A legal-size (8.5 by 14) page, unless it is an exhibit drawing or plat.
  • Six or more Property Identification Number references.
  • Six or more related document number references.

A plat filed alone is also non-standard. It must measure at least 11 by 17 inches and no more than 30 by 36, a range that takes in miscellaneous plats, easements and dedications.

A deed for a house on one parcel normally qualifies as standard when it is printed correctly. The higher fee tends to show up when a deed bundles several lots or cites a long list of earlier documents, so have the title agent count the parcel numbers before filing.

The RHSP surcharge

The $90.00 and $118.00 rates carry a $19.00 Rental Housing Support Program surcharge. The schedule drops that surcharge for documents recorded by federal, state or local government agencies, and the result is the $71.00 and $99.00 exempt rates.

A deed from a private seller is not a government filing, so the full rate applies. The exempt rows serve agencies, and state and federal documents are listed at $71.00. If it is unclear whether a filer counts as a government body, ask the office first so the check carries the right amount.

How the Illinois transfer tax is charged on a Will County sale

The state taxes the privilege of transferring title at 50 cents for every $500 of value, or fraction of $500, stated in the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). If the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the unpaid mortgage balance is left out of the base.

It is due even if no document is ever recorded, and it reaches related transactions as a group. The recorder collects it through revenue stamps (35 ILCS 200/31-15). Paper stamps were to be retired by December 31, 2025, with counties then issuing electronic stamps or similar indicia, and every sale recorded is reported to the Department of Revenue electronically.

Your contract decides who pays, and the settlement statement shows the line. Ask the Recorder and your municipality whether a local transfer tax applies in addition.

Deeds exempt from the transfer tax

Section 31-45 keeps a short, specific list of exemptions, and several entries touch homeowners and heirs.

  • Deeds with actual consideration under $100.

  • Tax deeds.
  • Deeds releasing property that secured a debt.
  • Deeds of partition.
  • Deeds given to a mortgage holder through foreclosure or a transfer in lieu of foreclosure.

The declaration is still required for some exempt deeds, such as certain governmental, charitable and exchange deeds, so an exemption does not always excuse the form.

Volume is the main story. Will County has 259,218 housing units, owners live in 82.8% of occupied homes, and builders pulled 1,993 permits in 2025, so new-construction deeds, plats and subdivision filings arrive alongside resales.

  2. List each Property Identification Number, keeping to five or fewer for the standard fee.
  3. Fill out the transfer declaration and settle the transfer tax with the office.
  4. Pay the fee and tax, then keep the stamped copy or confirmation.
  5. Order a certified copy at $42.00 if a lender or court wants one.

Before filing, settle property tax with the county Treasurer. Unpaid installments stay with the parcel and accrue interest under state law, so a payoff letter protects both buyer and seller.

When the title company handles the sale, expect the recording fee and transfer tax to appear as lines on the settlement statement. Check that the parcel number and legal description on the deed match your tax bill, since a mismatch is the most common reason a filing comes back for correction.

Does a quitclaim deed avoid the transfer tax?

Not automatically. The exemption list covers deeds with consideration under $100, correction deeds and certain others, and a deed with a higher stated value follows the normal rule.

Preparing a deed for recording

A deed that breaks a formatting rule is either billed at the non-standard rate or sent back. Real estate documents need the following:

  • White 8.5 by 11 inch paper, with the top 3 by 5 inches on the right side left blank.
  • No permanently bound or continuous forms, and nothing stapled or taped to a page.
  • The full name and address of the preparer, and of the place to return the document, within the text.
  • Original signatures and correct payment by check or cash.
  • For deeds, a complete name and address for where the tax bill is to be sent.
  • An associated document number for assignments and releases.

Plats have many rules of their own, so ask your surveyor. Fill in the tax bill address on the deed with care. The Treasurer's office warns that a bill can still reach the previous owner when the closing date and the recording date fall on different sides of a billing cycle.

MyDec and electronic recording

MyDec is the Illinois Department of Revenue's free online service for transfer declarations and revenue stamps, and Champaign County runs every property transaction through it. Each deed needs a signed and dated MyDec declaration or a letter of exemption. Set up your account before closing day, because the recorder checks the declaration as part of the package.

E-recording is the quick route. Documents sent through an approved partner go over the internet, get recorded and come back digitally the same day. The approved partners are ePN, Indecomm Global Services, Simplifile, CSC eRecording Solutions and Hopdox. Fewer rejections, faster corrections and no postage are the main perks, so ask your title company or settlement lawyer whether they file electronically.

Illinois transfer tax on a sale

The state charges a transfer tax of fifty cents per $500 of value, with any leftover fraction rounded up. The amount comes from the figures you enter on the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). Say the deed is made subject to a mortgage: then the balance still owed on that loan does not count toward the taxable amount. Recording is not what triggers the tax. It is owed even if the document never gets recorded.

The recorder collects through revenue stamps. Per 35 ILCS 200/31-15, paper stamps were to end on December 31, 2025, so counties now hand out electronic stamps or a similar marker that is reported through MyDec. Your settlement statement may carry local charges as well, and the Clerk and Recorder or your title company can tell you which.

Section 31-45 exempts certain deeds, including these:

  • Transfers involving a government body, or coming from some charitable, religious or educational groups.
  • Deeds given as security for a debt, and deeds releasing property held that way.
  • Corrective or confirming deeds that only repeat or fix one already on record.
  • Deeds with actual consideration under $100.
  • Tax deeds, partition deeds, and deeds delivered to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure.

Exempt does not always mean no paperwork. The declaration may still be required, so read the statute before you leave the form out.

Champaign County market context

The county had an estimated 209,972 residents by mid-2025 and covers about 996 square miles. Roughly 54.0% of housing units are owner-occupied, with a midpoint home value of $211,500 and midpoint rent of $1,051 a month. The University of Illinois sits between Urbana, the seat, and Champaign, the largest city.

The Clerk and Recorder works from the county's Urbana offices, and the Treasurer collects the tax on those same parcels from a different office. A student rental in Champaign, a ranch house in Mahomet and a farm parcel near a village all record the same way, but their prior-owner bills and unpaid installments can differ widely. Get the PIN history from the Treasurer before the deed goes in.

After the deed is recorded

Once the deed is on file, the land records show the new owner. Taxes run on a separate track. New owners should look to the closing papers, the title company or the attorney to learn whether anything is owed. When the bill lands with the former owner, it has to be forwarded. A duplicate is available from the Treasurer at 217-384-3743.

If you want a clean exit, make sure the settlement statement shows both of the year's installments as paid or credited. Anything unpaid goes to the annual sale in late October, and redeeming after that means a trip to the County Clerk.

Military discharge papers, liens and releases

Besides deeds, the office accepts DD-214 military discharge papers at no charge. Bring the original, and the staff will scan it, create a permanent record and hand the original back. A certified copy later requires a government-issued ID, and discharge papers less than 62 years old are not available to the public.

State and federal tax liens and releases are recorded for $51 each. A release for a mortgage you paid off is recorded here too, and it needs the document number of the mortgage it satisfies. Ask your title company to search for open mortgages and liens before you list, so any release can be recorded ahead of closing.

In a quick cash sale, ask the title company early what must be recorded and in what order. The deed, any release and any lien payoff are separate filings, each with its own fee and paperwork.

What does filing a deed cost in Champaign County?

$70 for a standard real estate document, or $82 if it misses one of the office's requirements. Fees rise by $10 on December 1, 2026.

Is a MyDec declaration required before a Champaign County deed is accepted?

Yes. Every deed needs a signed and dated MyDec declaration or a letter of exemption, and the county runs all property transactions through MyDec.

Can a deed be recorded electronically in Champaign County?

Yes. Approved partners such as Simplifile, ePN and CSC eRecording send documents over the internet, and they are recorded and returned the same day.

What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?

Fifty cents on each $500 of declared value, with any fraction counted as a full unit, under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. A mortgage balance left in place is excluded from the basis.

When is the recorder's office open?

Weekdays from 8 until 4:30, except major holidays. It opens at 9 on the second Wednesday of each month.

Where to record a deed in Lee County

Deeds are recorded by the Lee County Clerk and Recorder, whose office is one flight upstairs at the Old Lee County Courthouse, 112 E Second Street, Dixon. The staff there also handle vital records, assumed names, elections and delinquent taxes. Call 815-288-3309 or mail to P.O. Box 329, Dixon, IL 61021. Counter hours are 8 until half past four on weekdays, except legal holidays.

The county has 15,027 housing units, and 90.5% of residents had not moved in the prior year. People rarely leave, so a lot of local deeds come from inheritances, trusts and estates. Those files take more care.

Bring the vesting deed with you. Staff will not write a legal description for you. Copy it exactly from an earlier deed or a title report.

Lee County recording fees

The standard price for a warranty deed, quitclaim deed, mortgage release or similar paper is $88. If the document is exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, the charge is $69. The fee schedule took effect July 1, 2023 under 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1. A state act signed in February 2023 added $9 to the Rental Housing Support fee starting that July 1.

Pay with cash or check. The counter does not take debit or credit cards. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope, and send an original or certified copy, never a plain photocopy. Copies of a veteran's discharge are free. Transfer tax is a separate charge, covered below.

Page layout rules

Papers that follow the county's layout rules pay the standard fee, and anything that breaks them is charged $97. The rules:

  • Separate 8.5 by 11 inch sheets, unbound and not on a continuous form, with any attached graphic no larger than 11 by 17 inches.
  • Black ink that reads clearly, whether handwritten, typed or printed. Dates and signatures can be another color if they copy cleanly.
  • White stock, 20-pound weight or heavier, and leave a half inch of blank margin all the way around.
  • An empty 3 by 5 inch box in the top right corner of page one.
  • Nothing stapled or taped onto a page, though sheets can be stapled to each other.

Nobody at the recorder's counter or on its phone line can offer legal advice, write a legal description or run a title search. Take the description from your vesting deed or ask the title company, and let an attorney draft anything that transfers ownership.

Is a Plat Act affidavit part of a Lee County deed?

Almost always. Each deed needs a plat act affidavit or a stated exemption. Deeds inside the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision are the one exception, and the county's posted form for them declares the transfer exempt from the Illinois Plat Act (765 ILCS 205), with check boxes for the reason, for example a conveyance that leaves the parcel whole.

Deeds often get returned for lack of this affidavit. Selling only part of a lot or field? See the assessment office and a surveyor before anyone drafts, since dividing land is where the exemption breaks down.

Illinois transfer tax and the declaration

The state charges fifty cents on every $500 of value, rounding a partial $500 up, based on the number written on the declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). If the deed passes the property subject to a mortgage, that loan balance does not count toward the value. Counties collect the tax by selling revenue stamps (35 ILCS 200/31-15).

The declaration needs a signature from one seller and one buyer at minimum, or from their attorneys or agents. Deliver it with the deed, or inside 3 business days of the transfer if that comes first (35 ILCS 200/31-25). It asks about price, parcel number, legal description, deed type, address, improvements, any homestead exemptions on the latest bill, and whether the buyer and seller are related or the sale was compulsory.

Some deeds owe nothing: tax deeds, deeds with consideration under $100, and deeds handed to a lender in foreclosure or in place of it (35 ILCS 200/31-45). Several still need a declaration. The Clerk and Recorder can tell you whether a local charge applies besides the state tax.

After recording: the declaration's path

Staff keep the declaration apart from the deed. They note the deed's document number on it and send it to the chief county assessment officer within 30 days, and that office adds the assessed value and sends it to the Illinois Department of Revenue (35 ILCS 200/31-30). This is how assessment staff learn a Lee County parcel sold and for how much.

An accurate form protects both sides. It also affects the seller's homestead exemption: the credit carries through the assessment year in which you sell, and the next owner may be asked to apply for the year after (35 ILCS 200/15-175).

Electronic recording

E-recording is open only to approved submitters, from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. The county names four partners:

  • Corporation Service Company, at erecording.com
  • eRecording Partners Network, at goepn.com
  • Simplifile, at simplifile.com
  • Hopdox, at hopdox.com

Most title companies and closing attorneys file through one of these on the day of closing. A family transfer without a title company can go by mail, paper original plus check plus stamped return envelope, or be handed in at the counter. If you file on paper, call ahead so you know the exact total before you write the check.

Checks before the deed goes in

First look up the parcel on the county's property tax inquiry site and confirm who is the owner of record. Next, phone the Treasurer at 815-288-4477 and ask whether any year is unpaid or sold. When the buyer's title search turns up mortgages, liens or judgments, each has to be released of record or paid off at closing.

Inherited property adds steps. Whoever really holds title must sign as grantor, and that may be a personal representative who brings court papers. Repairs, tenants and back taxes do not change how recording works. They change who pays what at the closing table. A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the deed, declaration and fees stay the same.

A simple checklist for the counter: the signed and notarized deed, the signed transfer declaration, the plat act affidavit or exemption statement, the right fee by check or cash, and a return envelope. Calling ahead on anything unusual saves a second trip to Dixon.

It is $88, or $69 for a document exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee. Six or more parcel numbers, or breaking the layout rules, raises it to $97.

Does the Lee County recorder take credit cards?

No, only cash or check at the counter. Electronic filers use one of four approved partners.

How is Illinois transfer tax calculated?

Fifty cents per $500 of value, rounding up (35 ILCS 200/31-10). A loan the buyer assumes is excluded if the deed says the transfer is subject to it.

Does every Lee County deed need a plat affidavit?

All but deeds in the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision. The affidavit or a stated exemption is required, and the county website has the form.

When can a title company e-record in Lee County?

Filing is open from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. to approved submitters only. Those are Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hopdox.

About the Madison County Recorder

This office records, indexes and keeps every document that transfers land in the county. Its land record starts in 1812, the year the county was created. Besides deeds, mortgages, liens, trusts and easements, it records military discharge papers (DD-214) and out-of-county birth certificates and marriage licenses.

You will find it at 157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025, in the same building as the Treasurer and the Board of Review. The counter is open weekdays from half past eight to half past four, with holiday closures. Phone 618-296-4475 or email recorder@madisoncountyil.gov.

Recording is the step that puts a sale on the public record. Your title company or closing attorney normally files for you, but it helps to know what the office checks.

What a Madison County deed needs before recording

The office rejects a deed that misses state or county requirements. Each deed needs:

  • A completed Illinois Department of Revenue Real Estate Transfer Declaration (PTAX) or a Statement of Exemption.
  • The grantee's name and address for tax billing, required by 55 ILCS 5/3-5020. Madison is a county of the second class, with a population over 25,000 and not over 1,000,000.
  • A Plat Act Affidavit, with the form and instructions on the county website.
  • A permanent parcel number, which a county board resolution requires on every deed and document that transfers property.
  • The name and address of the person who should get the document back.
  • The name and address of whoever prepared the instrument, printed or stamped on its face (55 ILCS 5/3-5022). Court orders, wills, death certificates and instruments signed outside Illinois are excluded.

A release must also give the recorder's document number of the mortgage being released, or the book and page where applicable. The document number is preferred. If you pay by check, the office wants the recording fee and the transfer tax on separate checks.

Transfer tax

Two taxes apply to the declared price, each figured per $500 or part of $500 of taxable consideration. The State of Illinois collects $.50 and Madison County collects $.25. The full list of exemptions is available at the office, on the website and in 35 ILCS 200/31-45.

On the PTAX declaration you work out the net taxable consideration. The Department of Revenue supplies the forms, and the Recorder cannot take a deed and declaration until every required item is filled in. For help with the form, call the Recorder, or the state revenue agency's Springfield line at 217-782-4568.

Recording fees are separate and depend on the document type, so ask the office for the current fee schedule before you send payment.

Documents the office accepts

Deeds, mortgages and releases make up most of the volume, but the list is long. It covers warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, trustee's, executor's, administrator's, guardian's, conservator's, sheriff's and tax deeds, deeds in trust, easements, leases, contracts for deed, mortgage assignments and modifications, mechanic's liens, lis pendens, state and federal tax liens, plats and plats of survey, UCC filings and notices of probate.

Some categories carry their own rules:

  • Plats need the original plat and two copies, one mylar and one paper, plus a surveyor's certificate, a legal description, a school district statement and a 9-1-1 coordinator's certificate.
  • State tax liens trace to Chapter 35 ILCS, Act 5, Article 11, and federal tax liens come through the Internal Revenue Service.
  • A memorandum of judgment must show the court, date, amount, case number, the winning party and the last known address of the losing party.
  • Contracts for deed and sales contracts follow 765 ILCS 86/10-5.

Mortgage releases follow 765 ILCS 905/2. If you have an old mortgage, confirm the lender's release was recorded, because an unrecorded release can stall a closing.

Getting copies of recorded documents

Email copy requests to recordercopies@madisoncountyil.gov with the document's reference number. Staff do not run title searches, so the number is how they find it. Copies cost $1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, with a turnaround of 5 to 7 business days, though staff try to be quicker.

You can work out a reference from the parcel number on your tax bill. The county's format breaks down by township, land or lot, map, block and parcel. In the sample 14-2-15-10-20-303-007.001, the first 14 is the old township number, the 2 marks a subdivided lot, and 007 is the parcel with an 001 split suffix. Ending codes show the class: R00 for residential or farm, C00 commercial, A00 agricultural lease and D00 for TIF and enterprise zone parcels.

Taxes and the Recorder before you sell

Most tax work happens before the deed reaches the Recorder. Confirm with the Treasurer that your installments are paid. The Treasurer bills in July, September, October and December, so a closing between dates can leave a partly paid year. Put the buyer's tax bill address on the deed. The office will not record without it, and a wrong address sends the next bill astray.

The title search for your sale draws on a land record more than two centuries deep. If the house has problems, such as an unreleased old mortgage or a probate gap, ask the title company to check the Recorder's index early so they are fixed well ahead of closing.

Where the deed fits in a house sale

A typical sale follows a set order. The title company searches the Recorder's index, you sign a deed, the parties finish the PTAX declaration or claim an exemption, and the closer submits the package for recording. Transfer tax is figured from the declared consideration, and the state and county shares are collected together when the deed is accepted.

Because a deed missing required items is turned away, mistakes cost days. The usual culprits are a missing parcel number, no return address, no preparer statement, or a Plat Act Affidavit left out. Give your closer a tax bill showing the full parcel number, along with the buyer's mailing address, and you avoid most of them.

If the property is inside a subdivision, ask whether a plat covers it, since plats have their own recording rules. If you hold the home in a trust, say so at the start, because deeds in trust and trustee's deeds are separate document types. Heirs should bring the probate paperwork, since a notice of probate and an executor's or administrator's deed are also recorded here. A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but every item above still applies.

157 North Main Street, Suite 211, Edwardsville, IL 62025. Hours are weekdays from half past eight to half past four, with holiday closures.

The State of Illinois collects $.50 per $500 or part thereof of taxable consideration, and Madison County collects $.25 per $500 or part thereof. A PTAX declaration or exemption statement goes with the deed.

Do I need a parcel number on my deed?

Yes. A county board resolution requires a permanent parcel number on every deed and document that transfers property. Use the number printed on your tax bill.

How much does a copy of a recorded document cost?

$1 per page by mail or $2 per page by email, with a 5 to 7 business day turnaround. Include the reference number, since the office does not do title searches.

Does the deed need the buyer's address?

Yes. Illinois law requires the grantee's name and address for tax billing on a conveyance recorded in a county of the first or second class, and Madison is a second class county.

What the Recorder does

The Sangamon County Recorder is the official land records office for the county, and it permanently records deeds, mortgages, releases, assignments and liens. Its records go back to the early 1800s. It is a grantor and grantee office, meaning every record is found by the name of the seller or the buyer.

The office also stores subdivision plats, land surveys, veteran discharge papers and Uniform Commercial Code filings. Its job is to keep an accurate chain of title, which is the series of recorded documents that title companies review before a closing. The office is on the first floor of the County Building at 200 South Ninth Street in Springfield, and the main number is (217) 535-3150.

Recording fees

A standard deed costs $64 to record, and a non-standard document that carries the Rental Housing Support surcharge costs $84. State law HB3878 added $9.00 to the Rental Housing Support Fee in every Illinois county starting July 1, 2023.

The transfer tax stamp rate is $0.50 per $500 of value for the state plus $0.25 per $500 of value for the county. A sale of $100 or more requires a PTAX-203, the real estate transfer declaration, to accompany the deed so the tax can be set from the sale price.

  • A gift is exempt from transfer tax, but the deed must contain the matching exemption paragraph.

Documents are checked for statutory requirements and the fees are collected. They are recorded in the order received, given a document number, date and time, then scanned, indexed and verified.

Lien releases are recorded with the office as well, and a seller who has paid off a lien should make sure the release is on record before closing. Call the recorder if you are unsure whether a lien or release is on file.

Where St. Clair County deeds are recorded

Belleville is home to the St. Clair County Recorder of Deeds, and every deed for land inside the county goes there. State law (765 ILCS 5/28) ties recording to the county of the land, so a Belleville house is never recorded in Madison or Monroe County, whatever the seller's address.

The counter is staffed on weekdays starting at 8:30 AM and closing at 5:00 PM. Seven public workstations let anyone search the land records without charge, and a printout from those machines costs $2.00 per page.

The recorder prints a two-column price list. One column includes the RHSP surcharge and one leaves it out. Deeds, leases and easements carry transfer tax on top when it applies, and the office takes cash, or a check or money order written to Recorder of Deeds.

  • A tax deed or a deed of partition.
  • A deed to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu of it.

It asks for the value, parcel number, legal description, deed date, property address, type of improvement, lot size, related-party status and homestead exemptions on the last tax bill. A deed submitted without a complete declaration can be refused.

The parcel number also unlocks the county's online index, which wants it typed as 00-00-0-000-000. Copy it from your latest tax bill so the numbers match the record exactly.

Where a deed gets recorded

The Winnebago County Recorder's Office, Room 405 in the County Administration Building at 404 Elm Street, Rockford, IL 61101, files every deed for property in the county. Call (815) 319-4325. Service hours are weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

One office serves Rockford, Loves Park, South Beloit and every township around them. It holds deeds, mortgages, liens, plats and surveys, Uniform Commercial Code filings, corporation documents and military discharges, from hand-written volumes of the 1830s to the electronic index in use now.

The staff index and preserve what is handed in. Drafting is outside their role: they cannot help prepare a document or pick a deed type, and the most they will do is point out missing information when a document is presented. Plan on a lawyer or closing agent to draft the deed.

Recording fees

A document that meets the standard format is recorded for $54.00. That fee schedule started January 1, 2025. Payment can be cash, check or card, with no bill over $50 accepted.

The $12.00 extra applies when a document breaks the format rules or cites six or more parcel numbers or six or more document numbers. For plats, one full copy is all the office needs, and a missing copy adds $4.00 per page. Photocopies cannot be recorded, and each submission must show a name and address for return.

Deed format for the standard fee

The county's forms page repeats the state standard from 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.2. In plain terms:

  • Loose sheets of 8.5 by 11 inches, not bound for good and not a continuous form; attached graphics can run to 11 by 17.
  • Black ink throughout, by hand, typewriter or printer. Colored signatures and dates are fine if they copy clearly.
  • White stock rated 20 pounds or heavier, with half an inch of clear margin on the top, bottom and both sides.
  • The top right of page one left empty, in a space of 3 by 5 inches.
  • No staples or attachments fixed to any page.

Blank samples on the county site cover a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, a joint tenancy warranty deed, a tenancy by the entirety warranty deed and a Plat Act affidavit. The office gives no help filling them out, so have the attorney or title company complete the form.

MyDec and the Illinois transfer tax

Winnebago County has required an online transfer declaration from the state's MyDec portal since July 1, 2023, for any conveyance priced at $100 or more. Its status has to read "Closing Completed" when the deed is presented, and a paper PTAX-203 is refused. Anyone with internet access can prepare it in advance.

Separately, the state taxes the transfer itself, in Article 31 of the Property Tax Code (35 ILCS 200/31-1 to 31-70), and the county recorder collects the money. Section 31-15 prints the stamp rate as 50¢ per $500 of value or fraction of $500. Paper stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, with electronic stamps or other indicia after that. The final amount on a given sale follows the declaration, so your closing agent can quote it.

Searching land records

Phone searches are not offered. Visitors can ask at the front desk, or use the public stations when more than five searches are needed, and printed copies cost $0.50 per page.

  • Direct Search: free, limited, basic details only, with no images of documents.
  • Tapestry: pay as you go at $1.00 per printed page, with a per-search charge that the office sets and has raised before.
  • Laredo: set up for commercial users, and both Laredo and Tapestry sell subscriptions.
  • Mail and email requests: $10.00 per search for documents under 20 years old, $29.00 for older ones, and $10.00 plus $4.00 per page for plats. The cap is five searches per request, and email answers can take two business days.

For maps, WinGIS is the county's geographic information site, and the number for subscriptions is (815) 319-4450. A state database of Department of Revenue tax liens is also searchable online, which suits a pre-listing lien check.

Property Fraud Alert

Anyone can enroll at no cost. Give your name, pick phone, email or text, and you are notified each time a recorded document matches. It cannot block a filing, but it lets you react quickly if something is wrong, and a Spanish version exists.

State law adds a second layer. Public Act 104-0382, in force January 1, 2026, makes each county run a fraud referral and review process for recorded instruments. A deed that looks forged, altered or aimed at clouding title may be sent to administrative review.

Be wary of mailers that offer to sell you a copy of your deed. They do not come from any government office, and the same record can be had from the Recorder at the posted copy fees.

Deed and mortgage paperwork for sellers

Lenders do not hold the deed. The deed came back to the owner shortly after purchase, and the paper that shows a loan is satisfied is the Release of Mortgage, recorded in this same office. If you paid off a loan long ago and have no release, search the records now so a buyer's file is complete.

When the owner has died, get legal advice first. A new deed has to be prepared and recorded, and the Recorder cannot name the deed type. Typical order of work:

  1. Draft the deed to the format rules above.
  2. Finish the MyDec declaration until it shows "Closing Completed."
  3. Present the original, with a return address and the fee.
  4. File the recorded copy, plus any old mortgage release, with the closing papers.

A cash buyer working with a title company will usually handle these steps for you, but a missing release or a defective deed still has to be cured before the sale can record.

What to bring when you present a deed in person: the original signed deed, the finished MyDec declaration showing "Closing Completed," a name and address for return, and payment by cash, check or card. Remember that the office will not accept a bill over $50 and will not record a photocopy. If the document breaks a format rule, the fee rises to $66.00, so a quick check of margins, ink and the blank 3 by 5 inch space on page one is worth a minute before you hand it over. After recording, ask for the recorded copy and keep it with your closing papers, since a buyer's lender or a later title search will want the same record.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Winnebago County fee for a standard deed?

$54.00. A deed that breaks the format rules or names six or more parcel numbers is $66.00, and veteran discharge papers record free.

Is the paper PTAX-203 still accepted in Winnebago County?

No. Conveyances of $100 or more need a MyDec declaration that reads Closing Completed.

Will the Winnebago County Recorder draft a deed for me?

No. Drafting and choosing a deed type are outside the office's role, and staff only note missing information at presentation.

Where can I get a recorded Winnebago County deed copy?

At the counter, through the online search sites, or by mail or email request. Plain copies are $0.50 per page; certified copies are $35.00 per document.

Can I be warned when something is recorded against my property?

Yes. Enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert and a matching recording triggers a phone, email or text notice.
